problem: The sentence 'with more time or space, strictly more languages are decidable' is loose. Because TIME and SPACE are defined with O(), doubling the bound gives the same class; for time the theorem needs the larger bound to exceed the smaller by about a log factor, and 'decidable' suggests decidability rather than membership in the class.
fix: Say: for space-constructible bounds, a strictly larger space bound gives strictly more languages; for time the same holds once the larger bound exceeds the smaller by a log factor (for example TIME(n²) is strictly larger than TIME(n), while TIME(2n) equals TIME(n)). The languages in these classes are all decidable; it is the class that grows.

where: Worked example 1, steps 3 and 4 and the dry-run table
problem: Step 3 counts 'cells scanned' and step 4 turns that into 'total steps', and the table repeats the same number under both columns. Time counts head moves, which can exceed distinct cells scanned when the head revisits cells; the two are only equal here because each round is one sweep right and one sweep left. A student may take 'steps = cells scanned' as a general rule.
fix: Say: each round makes at most 2n head moves (a rightward sweep of at most n moves and a leftward sweep of at most n moves), so total moves are at most k × 2n = 3 × 12 = 36 = n². The number of distinct cells scanned in a round is also at most 2n, but it is the moves that count as time.

problem: The bullet TIME(f(n)) ⊆ SPACE(f(n)) 'for f(n) ≥ n' sits inside the discussion of the read-only input tape model. In that model the condition f(n) ≥ n is unnecessary: a machine running f steps touches at most f + 1 work cells for any f. The condition belongs only to the single-tape model where input cells count as space.
fix: Add the model to the bullet: 'On a single tape, where input cells count as space, TIME(f(n)) ⊆ SPACE(f(n)) for f(n) ≥ n. With a read-only input tape the same inclusion holds for every f, because only work cells count.'
